posts.title: Mabel, dachshund, small bed in Custard
posts.content: Mabel measured 52 cm nose to tail, so she got a small. She spends most of the day on it and the rest of the day guarding it from the cat.
posts.excerpt: Mabel measured 52 cm nose to tail, so she got a small.

posts.title: Kevin, pug, brass name tag
posts.content: Kevin's tag says KEVIN on the front, which Kevin's owner says is mainly for the benefit of other dogs. Photo taken by the river in Faversham, after a swim he did not plan.
posts.excerpt: Kevin's tag says KEVIN, mainly for the benefit of other dogs.

posts.title: Doris, whippet, stole a lettuce blanket
posts.content: This is not one of our blankets. Doris's owner sent it anyway, because she wanted us to know about the competition. We have put it on the wall as a warning to ourselves.
posts.excerpt: Not our blanket. Posted as a warning to ourselves.

posts.title: Otis, Shih Tzu, collar in Pool
posts.content: Otis wears an XS collar in Pool and has never given back a tennis ball in his life. Sent in by Rukhsana from Whitstable.
posts.excerpt: XS collar in Pool. Has never given back a tennis ball.

posts.title: Bramble, lurcher cross, crate mat
posts.content: Bramble's crate is an Ellie-Bo 36 inch, so she has the 91 × 58 cm mat in Tennis ball green. She sleeps in the crate with the door open, by choice.
posts.excerpt: Ellie-Bo 36 inch crate, 91 × 58 cm mat in green.

posts.title: Nell, border collie, orange lead
posts.content: Nell has the 1.8 m lead in Marmalade and a medium collar to match. Her owner, Callum, says the lead is the only one he has not lost on Dartmoor.
posts.excerpt: 1.8 m lead in Marmalade. Not yet lost on Dartmoor.

posts.title: Biscuit, rescue, medium bed, never uses it
posts.content: Biscuit came from the Thanet rescue in March. We sent a medium bed in Bubblegum. Her owner sent us this photo of where she actually sleeps.
posts.excerpt: We sent a medium bed. This is where she actually sleeps.

posts.title: Moose, whippet, sighthound collar
posts.content: Moose had backed out of three collars before this one. The martingale loop means it tightens a little when he pulls back, so he stays put. His owner says the park is a calmer place now.
posts.excerpt: Backed out of three collars before this one.
